editorial:
You follow a smart teen and his friends who find old blueprints for a time machine, build it, and start fixing small mistakes. The found-footage style puts you right in their garage and school halls, so it feels like hanging out with them. It is energetic, a little messy, and full of teen excitement that makes the sci-fi feel personal. The story moves fast, and the friendships feel real, so you care when things go wrong.

The cast sells the wonder and panic, and the time jumps keep you guessing. It can get confusing near the end, and the camera shakes a lot. The effects are simple but effective, and the soundtrack keeps the energy high. Still, if you like sci-fi thrillers with heart, this is a fun ride. It is not perfect, but it is easy to enjoy with friends. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for movie night.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the teen realizes every change made things worse, including a deadly accident. He goes back to the day they found the plans and stops himself from building the machine. The timeline resets, and he loses the memories and friendships tied to time travel. The last shot shows him meeting the girl again, hinting at a fresh start without the machine.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves teen sci-fi adventures and time travel stories.
